newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm in thin trade.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended slightly firmer on Wednesday after remaining confined to their early range as activity dwindled in the afternoon.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract added 55 points to 18,475 after hitting a low of 18,205. Market turnover was a light 13,235 lots.
Dealers said the market largely shrugged off a 25 basis point rate hike by the Federal Reserve as it had been priced in and even Wall Street had a muted response to the news.
"The liquidity just dried up in the afternoon. It looks like there's a lot of resistance around 18,500," said a trader with a Japanese futures house.

He said worries about a possible change in the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s monetary policy would inhibit gains and the June contract was likely to trade between 18,000 and 18,700 until the central bank's quarterly business sentiment survey next week.
"Dollar/yen is at a March high now and if the market charges up, the BOJ will have no choice but to raise rates," he added.

The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 340.0 against its opening 329.5 on volume of 562 lots. April saw almost double the turnover and ended at 336.3 against 322.5 ahead of March's expiry on Friday.
